skill.name: aiops
skill.description: Generic AIOps patterns for monitoring, observability, incident response, predictive analysis, and self-healing automation. The skill gives framework-agnostic examples for platform teams using Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger, Datadog, Kubernetes, and SLO workflows.
skill.summary: Implement framework-agnostic AIOps patterns for monitoring, automation, and observability.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown fence false positives, but the automation section contains real kubectl command execution through asyncio.create_subprocess_exec. The Datadog example handles API keys and builds an outbound API URL from a configurable site value, which can expose credentials if reused without endpoint validation. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Automation examples execute kubectl commands from action parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Add target allowlists, namespace validation, approval gates, dry-run mode, and audit logging before command execution.

remediation.issue: Datadog credentials are attached to a session built from a configurable site.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the site against approved Datadog domains and document secret storage requirements before sending API headers.

remediation.issue: The notification example accepts arbitrary webhook destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Require approved webhook URLs and redact incident details before sending outbound notifications.

content.value_statement: Modern operations teams need reliable patterns for monitoring, incident response, and self-healing automation. This skill provides framework-agnostic AIOps designs, examples, and workflows.
actual_capabilities: Defines a generic AIOps engine for alerts, metrics, logs, traces, and response plans.
Shows integrations for Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger, and Datadog data sources.
Provides anomaly detection, log analysis, and capacity prediction patterns.
Outlines automation handlers for scaling, restart, patch, notification, suppression, isolation, and failback actions.
Covers observability dashboards, service health reports, SLO checks, and error budgets.
limitations: Examples are reference patterns, not a packaged production library.
Kubernetes command examples need validation, authorization, and approval controls before real use.
Monitoring integrations require platform credentials and endpoint configuration.
Machine learning examples require training data, tuning, and operational testing.

use_cases.title: Design Platform Monitoring
use_cases.description: Create a platform monitoring architecture that combines metrics, logs, traces, and alert enrichment.

use_cases.title: Plan Incident Automation
use_cases.description: Draft automated response workflows for common incidents, including retries, timeouts, notifications, and rollback checks.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Reliability
use_cases.description: Define SLO tracking, error budget reporting, and service health views for operations reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Map an AIOps Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the aiops skill to design a simple AIOps architecture for my services. Include data sources, alert flow, and response steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Monitoring Integrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the aiops skill to compare Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger, and Datadog integrations for this environment. Recommend data models and query boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Incident Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the aiops skill to create an incident automation workflow for repeated service failures. Include approval gates, rollback checks, and observability signals.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Self-Healing Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the aiops skill to review this self-healing design for production readiness. Focus on command safety, credential handling, audit logs, and failure modes.

output_examples.input: Create a response plan for high CPU incidents.
output_examples.output: A concise plan with alert enrichment steps, scaling criteria, rollback checks, notification rules, and human approval points.

output: Service health panels for latency, errors, saturation, and availability.
SLO compliance views with error budget burn rates.
Incident context sections linking alerts, logs, and traces.

output_examples.output: A workflow covering data collection, trend analysis, risk scoring, capacity recommendations, and validation against historical incidents.

best_practices: Validate all automation targets and parameters before executing remediation actions.
Keep credentials in approved secret stores and restrict outbound endpoints.
Test anomaly models with historical incidents before enabling automated response.
anti_patterns: Running remediation commands from untrusted alert data without approval.
Sending API keys to configurable or unvalidated monitoring endpoints.
Treating sample machine learning thresholds as production defaults.

faq.question: Does this skill run infrastructure commands itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference patterns in SKILL.md, but examples include commands that need controls before implementation.

faq.question: Which monitoring platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger, and Datadog integration patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a complete AIOps product?
faq.answer: No. It is a pattern guide for designing and implementing AIOps workflows.

faq.question: What security controls should I add first?
faq.answer: Start with credential storage, endpoint allowlists, target validation, approval gates, and audit logging.

faq.question: Does it include SLO and error budget guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The observability section includes SLO checks, service health reports, and error budget calculations.
